question: Why does that shirt match indoors and clash outside?
answer: Because colour vision takes only three samples of a continuous spectrum. Two objects reflecting quite different light can produce identical signals — a metameric match — under one light and separate under another. The colours did not change. The sampling did.
move: Two colours can be the same colour, until you carry them to a window.
reference: Wyszecki & Stiles, Color Science: Concepts and Methods, Quantitative Data and Formulae, Wiley, 1982
